Add CCSR categories to a NIS query

Source: R/ccsr-query.R
nis_add_ccsr.Rd

Matches complete ICD-10 codes in DuckDB and preserves one row per input row. The "any" and "principal" positions produce a list column of distinct, sorted categories. For inpatient diagnoses, "default" produces the single HCUP default category for I10_DX1.

Usage

nis_add_ccsr(
  .data,
  categories = NULL,
  type = c("dx", "pr"),
  position = c("any", "principal", "default"),
  version = NULL,
  name = "ccsr"
)

Arguments

.data

Lazy DuckDB query with YEAR and canonical I10_DX<n> or I10_PR<n> slots. When present, DQTR identifies Q4 2015 and DXVER or PRVER must be 10 or missing for ICD-10 records.

categories

Optional character vector of CCSR category codes, such as "CIR019", to keep. The default returns all assigned categories.

type

"dx" for diagnoses or "pr" for procedures.

position

"any" checks all slots, "principal" checks slot 1, and "default" returns the inpatient principal diagnosis default.

version

Optional bundled version, such as "2025.1", to use across years.

name

Name of the new column.

Value

A lazy DuckDB query with one additional column.

Details

AHRQ's CCSR mappings are cumulative from October 2015. For each discharge year, the default is the earliest bundled fiscal year covering that entire calendar year, using the latest bundled revision of that fiscal year. The bundled DXCCSR and PRCCSR v2025.1 cover Q4 2015 and 2016–2024 by this rule. Pinning "2025.1" also covers Q1–Q3 2025 when DQTR is available. A fixed version can keep category definitions constant across years.

ICD-9 discharges and rows outside the selected release's coverage get missing results. Within coverage, a row without any matching codes gets an empty list, or NA for its inpatient default category. Match results use the release as published and do not establish whether an individual code was valid on a specific discharge date.

See also

nis_ccsr_codes(), AHRQ HCUP CCSR.

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpIiHPDo/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpIiHPDo/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
nis |>
  nis_add_ccsr(position = "default") |>
  dplyr::count(ccsr) |>
  dplyr::collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   ccsr       n
#>   <chr>  <dbl>
#> 1 CIR019   108
#> 2 RSP002    84
